claim: `rename-page-property-property-slug` says every file a file property's key names is carried to the name the new key spells, and it does that for a file property. It does not do it for a page property entry, whose rows also sit in a file beside the page named for the key. Renaming `snapshots` to `readings` on `temper-net-worth-hour` wrote the new key on all 873 hour pages and moved none of the 873 `.snapshots.jsonl` files, so every one of those folders then matched no folder shape and the landing was refused whole. The change answers, the refusal comes from the checks, and nothing between them says the files were left behind.

evidence:
MEASURED 2026-09-19 against `temper/holdings/temper-net-worth-hour`. A drafting `akasha change apply --draft rename-page-property-property-slug` naming that property answered 874 `changes` lines and 0 `moves` lines: 873 hour pages plus the property's own page. `akasha change list` over those kept edits held no move either. The same call over a file property does move its file, which is what the change's own decision `Every file a file property's key names is carried to the name the new key spells` states.

WHAT THE CHECKS SAID. Applying the kept edits was refused with one entry per hour page, each of the form `temper/holdings/temper-net-worth-hour/pages/hour-2026-04-29-14 — this folder matches no folder shape — ... as a-page-with-its-parts, 1 files are no part of `hour-2026-04-29-14`: hour-2026-04-29-14.temper-net-worth-hour.snapshots.jsonl`. The refusal names the file left behind, so the evidence is in the answer, but it is one line per page over 873 pages and it runs past what one answer holds.

THE SHAPE OF THE GAP. A page property entry declares rows a page keeps beside itself, stated on the page as `snapshots: "jsonl"`. The key on the page and the name of the file are one name in two places, exactly as a file property's are. The change rewrites the first and leaves the second.

ORDERING ALSO MATTERS AND IS NOT SAID. `move-property-on-every-page` reads the world the kept edits leave, so a run that renames the property page first is answered `a `temper-net-worth-hour` has no property under `snapshots``. The rows have to move before the property page is renamed, and nothing says so.

WHAT IS LEFT. The edits were dropped and the tree is as it was, so `temper-net-worth-hour` still states `snapshots` where its page type and its property page's own definition both say reading. The next entry shape whose key is renamed will do this again.
